messages:
luke (oncall-sre): heads up — us-east1 GPU pool capacity down ~18%, autoscaler started mass-drains around 07:12. getting client errors and increased retries.

maya (ml-infra): i'm seeing a huge spike in prometheus ECC counters for many GPUs. suspicious — host-level ECC logs don't show matching HW resets.

sam (eng-infra): we rolled out prometheus-exporter v2.5.0 @07:05 to us-east1. exporter introduced a new label and a metric rename; possible recording rule mismatch.

rahul (eng-sre): autoscaler has a drain rule: if ECC > 10 in 5m per-gpu -> cordon+drain. if prometheus duplicated series it could create noisy high counts per-gpu and trigger mass drains.

ops-bot: Alert: ECC_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED - us-east1-gpu - 07:12 - hosts affected: 42 - action: auto-drain

maya (ml-infra): logs:
```
# query
sum by(instance) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))
# result showed weird duplication across label gpu_index
```

sam (eng-infra): repro steps — exporter introduced `gpu_index` label and our recording rule accidentally multiplied series when we rewrote aggregation. Rule that caused the problem:
```
record: cluster:gpu:ecc:rate
expr: sum by (instance, gpu_index) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))
```
should have collapsed gpu_index for node-level metric. This exploded counts.

luke (oncall-sre): timeline — autoscaler threshold triggered, drained nodes sequentially causing capacity drop and some requests moved to dedicated fallback in other regions, spiking cross-region egress and cost — finance alerted.

maya (ml-infra): confirmed cost impact: cross-region fallback increased egress and on-demand burst use; rough estimate ~$12k extra in last 2 hours.

rahul (eng-sre): mitigation plan:
- disable autoscaler auto-drain policy for gpu ECC immediately (manual override) -> done
- rollback prometheus-exporter v2.5.0 in us-east1 -> in progress
- run cleanup: uncordon nodes drained by false-positive -> manual validation first
- add guard: change rule to require physical ECC metric corroboration + sustained window

sam (eng-infra): executing rollback now, will patch recording rule to remove gpu_index aggregation bug, then re-evaluate nodes.

ops-bot: Action: autoscaler auto-drain disabled by rahul at 07:28

maya (ml-infra): i'm running a script to diff exporter output vs host logs to make sure we don't miss real hardware faults.

luke (oncall-sre): oncall: please don't uncordon nodes until we've confirmed no real ECC hardware issues. we will prioritize nodes with host-level reset logs for replacement.

sam (eng-infra): rolling patch applied to prometheus recording rules, will restart prom-querier in us-east1 in 2m.

rahul (eng-sre): creating incident INC-2026-05 and assigning postmortem to eng-infra + ml-infra. will include cost estimate and action items.

maya (ml-infra): postmortem note: telemetry safety — always cross-check device-level hw metrics before automated remediation. also add synthetic canary for exporter changes.

sam (eng-infra): ETA for full recovery: 30-45m depending on propagation.

luke (oncall-sre): thanks. marking thread for follow-ups; notify product and finance about temporary cost spike. :folded_hands: 

finance: noted — please tag any cost events w/ invoice code `INC-2026-EAST1`.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-05 created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-05

rahul (eng-sre): last checks ok so far, will update when nodes start getting uncordoned. keeping autoscaler disabled until postmortem.

sam (eng-infra): rollback finished, prometheus metrics look sane now. we see ECC counts back to baseline.

maya (ml-infra): starting validation run to uncordon nodes in small batches (3 nodes at a time) and monitor for real ECC signals.

luke (oncall-sre): last update: capacity restored to ~99% after controlled uncordons and drains reversed. closing alert but keeping incident open for postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-05 status: monitoring
